In order to understand many of the terms used in 3-phase power distribution systems, you must first know how the alternator windings are connected. 1. WYE 2. DELTA
Three phase systems are usually WYE connected for military applications. 1. WYE
The term "WYE" is derived from the shape of the connection.
One lead of each armature winding is connected together to a common or neutral line, which is usually grounded.
The other three leads are called "Phase Voltages", labeled A, B and C.
Since each phase has a common ground (neutral), any one phase can be used to power single-phase loads.
Most high power transmission lines are 3-phase WYE connected.
Your home appliances run on single phase AC................
LINE VOLTAGE, is the voltage between any two phases: A to B, B to C and C to A.
There is a simple conversion between line voltages and phase voltage. WYE Connection Line Voltage = Phase Voltage x 1.73 Line Current = Phase Current
TDX OPERATIONAL CHECK
Tracing current paths, one can see that line current is the same as phase current.
The second type of 3-phase power connection is called the "DELTA" connection. 1. WYE 2. DELTA
Notice that a DELTA connection has no neutral and also uses only three wires.
For a DELTA connection, one end of two armature coils are connected together and the output is taken across any one phase. Va = Phase C Line Ra A Rc Vc = Phase Line
In the DELTA connection, line voltage and phase voltage are equal.
In a DELTA connection, it is the currents which are out of phase and there is a conversion factor. Delta Connection Line Voltage = Phase Voltage Line Current = 1.73 x Phase Current

Balanced means the resistor values are the same. This implies the voltage across each phase resistor is equal. R = Ra = Rb = Rc
Since current is determined by phase voltage and resistance, line current will equal phase current. Any difference results in neutral current. Phase V = Ia = Ib = Ic Phase R R = Ra = Rb = Rc
